messages:
Nora: Heads-up: post-launch backlog triage for the next micro-sprint. We have a customer-facing SLA regression (worker restart storms) vs a list of 5 small UX/analytics fixes. Need a quick call on priority.
Ilya: Regression detail: p99 latency spikes and ~0.8% error increase after the autoscaler tweak. Affected 3 tenants. Root cause likely aggressive scale-down policy.
Cam: UX/analytics items: 1) dashboard retention label fix (2h), 2) export CSV edge-case (4h), 3) onboarding checklist alignment (3h), 4) missing tags in metrics (3h), 5) docs update for quotas (1h). Most are quickwins.
QA-Li: SLA regression is P1 for those customers. Acceptance for any mitigation: stable p99 within 15% of baseline and error delta <= 0.1% in canary window.
PM-Sam: Business says prioritize customer SLA if mitigation is <=2 dev-days and doesn't block other high-impact work. Otherwise, prefer quickwins and communicate tradeoffs.
Nora: Two mitigation options: A) tweak autoscaler cooldown and add guardrail (est 1.5d). B) revert autoscaler change (ops flip) which takes ~3h but loses auto-scale improvements.
Ilya: Revert is fastest and reversible. Guardrail keeps gains but needs dev time and tests. I can ship the guardrail in 36-48h if we commit.
Cam: If we go revert, can we still fit 2-3 quickwins into the micro-sprint? Designers say retention label + docs are highest impact.
PM-Sam: Proposal: do the revert now to stop customer pain, ship top 2 quickwins this sprint (retention label, docs), then schedule guardrail/autoscaler follow-on as an epic: "autoscale-guardrails" estimate 6d.
CS-Rachel: I'll prepare customer comms: mitigation applied + plan to reinstate improved autoscaling once guardrails land. They'll want ETA.
QA-Li: Test plan for revert: smoke canary 12h, run customer repro traces, verify p99 and error metrics.
Nora: Owners: Ilya for revert (ops), Cam for retention label + docs, PM-Sam for comms, QA-Li for tests. Follow-on epic owner: Ilya.
EngOpsBot: Canary window requested: 2024-11-05T07:00Z for service "autoscaler". Auto-rollback threshold: 0.3% error over baseline.
Ilya: Opening revert branch `ops/revert-autoscale-2024-11` -> https://github.com/redwood/control-plane/pull/1210 (WIP). ETA: ops flip in 3h after approvals.
Cam: Creating tickets: PROD-9001 (retention-label), DOC-404 (autoscale-docs). PRs small, will link once ready.
QA-Li: Will add canary assertions and a replay of the 3 tenant traces once revert is live.
Ilya: Revert applied to canary. Monitoring now.
EngOpsBot: Canary started at 2024-11-05T07:05Z. Monitoring hooks: #prod-alerts.
QA-Li: Canary 6h check: p99 improved from +18% -> +3% vs baseline; error delta down to 0.08%. Continuing 12h run.
PM-Sam: I'll notify the customers that we reverted the change and plan a guarded re-release. Attachment: link to follow-on epic and tentative timeline.
Nora: Backlog housekeeping: create epic "autoscale-guardrails" tagged "follow-on:infrastructure" and move the remaining 3 quickwins into the sprint backlog if Cam confirms capacity.
Cam: Confirmed. I'll push the two quickwins now and try to squeeze the metrics tags if time allows.
CS-Rachel: Customers acknowledged the mitigation and asked to be looped when the guardrail epic has an ETA.
Ilya: If canary stays green at 12h, we'll promote to prod in the scheduled window. If not, we'll keep revert and escalate.
EngOpsBot: Canary 12h: metrics stable. Proceeding to scheduled prod rollout at 2024-11-05T20:00Z.
Nora: Decision recap: revert autoscaler change (ops flip) to mitigate SLA regression, ship top 2 quickwins this sprint, schedule autoscale-guardrails as follow-on epic (owner Ilya, est 6d). Owners/acceptance noted. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
